title: Cambodia–Thailand trade slumps as imports from Thailand plunge nearly 50% in January 2026

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet emphasized that safeguarding territorial integrity and citizens is the government's 'supreme priority.' He reaffirmed that the border is an international boundary protected by the UN Charter and stated Cambodia will not recognize any border alterations made through force. He insisted on a peaceful resolution through international law and existing colonial-era maps.
title: People and territory come first for Cambodia, PM says

summary: Khmer Times reported an Interior Ministry update covering February 10–11: another 1,240 displaced people had returned home, bringing total returnees to nearly 560,000, or 87% of more than 640,000 displaced by the fighting. The ministry said 82,306 people remained in camps, including 43,283 women and 27,667 children. It also reported continuing school and health-facility closures in Oddar Meanchey, Banteay Meanchey and Preah Vihear.
title: Hun Manet calls for unity as thousands remain displaced

summary: On February 11, the Cambodian Mine Action Authority responded to Thai social-media reports citing Thai military claims about anti-personnel mines found along the border. CMAA said Cambodia complies with its Ottawa Convention obligations, does not produce, stockpile or use anti-personnel mines, and assessed that mines found in those border areas were remnants of past wars. It warned that claims made without clear sourcing or verification could increase tensions.
title: Cambodian Mine Authority Reaffirms Ottawa Convention Commitments and Clarifies Border Mine Findings

summary: Reuters reported on February 11 that Cambodian anti-scam official Chhay Sinarith said authorities had sealed about 190 scam-centre locations in recent weeks, arrested 173 senior figures and deported about 11,000 workers in a campaign that began late in 2025. Reuters separately noted that Thai forces had bombed and occupied an O'Smach scam compound during the December border fighting.
title: Cambodia says it has closed almost 200 scam centers in fraud crackdown

summary: Keo Remy, Chairman of the Cambodian Human Rights Committee, met with Japanese Ambassador Ueno Atsushi. The Cambodian side accused Thailand of ongoing aggression and military occupation despite the Dec 2025 ceasefire. They reported that 90,000 displaced Cambodians still cannot return home because Thai troops are using shipping containers and barbed wire to block them. The ambassador reportedly promised to relay these concerns to the new Japanese government.
title: Keo Remy: Japanese Ambassador promises to relay border dispute issues to new Tokyo government

summary: The Cambodian Mine Action and Victim Assistance Authority (CMAA) rejected implications that Cambodia laid new mines after Thai forces reported finding an 'encroaching' Cambodian base and a MBV-78A2 landmine in Trat province. CMAA stated that Cambodia follows international treaties and any mines found are legacy devices from past conflicts, warning that unverified claims could increase unnecessary tensions.
title: Thai Military Finding of Border Anti-Personnel Mines Are Likely Legacy Device, Cambodia Asserts

summary: A Thai private, Pariwat Meemana, was severely injured after stepping on an anti-personnel landmine at Chong Sa-ngam, Phu Sing District, Si Sa Ket province. The blast resulted in the loss of his lower left leg and shrapnel wounds to his right leg. This area has been a flashpoint for recent tensions. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul acknowledged the incident, stating the mines are old remnants from previous occupations. Local traders are terrified that this will trigger a 'third round' of armed clashes.
title: URGENT: Thai Soldier Loses Leg in Landmine Blast Near Cambodian Border

summary: On February 11, the Cambodian Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a strong protest against the Thai military for destroying civilian infrastructure and administrative buildings in the Boeung Trakuon area (between markers 33-36) and digging canals and building roads in Chouk Chey village (between markers 46-47). Cambodia views these as attempts to create 'facts on the ground' to legitimize illegal occupation.
title: Cambodia protests against Thai actions destroying administrative buildings at Boeung Trakuon and digging canals in Cambodian land

summary: Groups of Cambodian students and youth have expressed public outrage over what they describe as the continued Thai occupation of border provinces despite the ceasefire. Protesters are calling on the government to take faster action to reclaim territory and remove Thai blockades that prevent local villagers from accessing their homes and farms. The report captures rising nationalist sentiment among the younger generation following reports of Thai military infrastructure expansion.
title: Students denounce Thai blockade of Cambodian territory

summary: Dr. Kun Nhem, Director General of Customs and Excise, stated on February 12 that Cambodia has not faced shortages or high inflation despite the land border closure and a ban on strategic Thai imports like fuel, gasoline, and diesel. He noted that while imports from Thailand have plunged, customs revenue in 2025 actually increased by 21% due to internal efforts and diversification.
title: Closing border with Thailand has not caused Cambodia to lack goods or increase inflation

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, visited Cambodia to assess the border situation in Banteay Meanchey. Representing the ASEAN chair, he met with PM Hun Manet and confirmed the Philippines' readiness to lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to facilitate a peaceful and impartial resolution to the ongoing dispute.
title: ASEAN chair Philippines monitoring Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: Recent international reports shared by Thai media reveal the inner workings of Chinese-run scam centers in Cambodia that have finally been shut down. Investigators found 'scripts' specifically designed to target Thai citizens. While Cambodian authorities have ramped up crackdowns recently, the report notes that past efforts were often seen as insufficient, and the current campaign aims to arrest high-level ringleaders to reduce regional friction.
title: Exposed: Shuttered Scam Bases in Cambodia Found With Scripts to Defraud Thais

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, met with PM Hun Manet on February 12 to confirm that the Philippines is ready to lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT), taking over from Malaysia. The team is tasked with verifying and monitoring the ceasefire along the border. Hun Manet updated the delegation on recent tensions and reiterated Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful resolution based on international law and the Franco-Siamese maps.
title: Philippines ready to lead AOT to resolve Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: Government spokesman Pen Bona accused Thai armed forces of 'unlawful activities' in Banteay Meanchey, including destroying civilian infrastructure near Boundary Pillars 33-36 and filling ponds to alter the terrain. Bona stated these actions are attempts to 'legitimize unlawful occupation' and reaffirmed that Cambodia will only accept borders defined by the 1904-1907 Franco-Siamese treaties.
title: Government Spokesman Says Cambodia Opposes Any Change to Borders by Force

summary: General Vong Pisen, Commander-in-Chief of the Royal Cambodian Armed Forces, met with Philippine counterpart Gen. Romeo S. Brawner Jr. in Phnom Penh. The Philippine general praised the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and expressed a commitment to mediate the 'fragile' border dispute neutrally. He is scheduled to personally inspect the Banteay Meanchey border on February 13 to better understand the situation.
title: Philippine Military Chief Pledges Neutrality in Efforts to Resolve Cambodia-Thailand Border Dispute

summary: On February 12, Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul authorized stronger border fences and military modernization after a Thai soldier stepped on a landmine in Sisaket on February 11. He also said MOU 44 could be cancelled by Cabinet resolution without parliamentary approval, framing that as a legal-process point rather than announcing that cancellation had already occurred.
title: PM Greenlights Military to Strengthen Border Fences and Weapons; Says Cabinet Can Cancel 2001 MOU

summary: Following the 2025 border conflict and trade disruptions, Cambodia is drastically reducing its economic reliance on Thailand. Imports of essential goods, particularly fuel which previously came 90% from Thailand, are now being rerouted through Vietnam and China. This strategic shift has caused logistics costs to rise by 25-40%, but is seen as a move toward strategic independence from Thailand.
title: Cambodia shifts economic reliance to Vietnam and China amid border crisis

summary: The Royal Thai Army defended its decision to build a border fence and upgrade military equipment, stating these are standard measures to combat transnational crime and illegal crossings. The Thai-Cambodia Situation Information Centre denied rumors of severing diplomatic ties, emphasizing that Thailand remains committed to resolving border issues through the Joint Border Commission (JBC) and military channels.
title: Thai military clarifies border fence, defense upgrades after Cambodia protests

summary: Cambodian media outlets have reportedly reacted with concern to PM Anutin's proposal to cancel MOU 2001. Analysts in Phnom Penh suggest that unilateral action by Thailand could have severe diplomatic and legal consequences, with some sources threatening to take the matter to the UN or the International Court of Justice. The report highlights the rising tension and the fragile state of bilateral relations following Thailand's recent general election.
title: Cambodia Alarmed! Warns Thailand of Damaging Relations After Anutin's Move to Cancel MOU 44

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., chief of staff of the Philippines armed forces, met with Cambodian PM Hun Manet in Phnom Penh on Thursday. As the current ASEAN chair, the Philippines confirmed it is closely monitoring the situation and will lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to maintain peace. Hun Manet reaffirmed Cambodia's commitment to a peaceful resolution based on international law and the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Asean chair Philippines monitoring border issue, AOT will continue to facilitate resolution

summary: The Philippine Armed Forces Chief, General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., visited the Cambodia-Thailand border to monitor the situation. The visit signals the Philippines' active role as the 2026 ASEAN Chair in leading the ASEAN Observers Team (AOT) to mediate the dispute.
title: ASEAN Chair Philippines Inspects Banteay Meanchey Border

summary: A landmine explosion on February 11 in Thailand's Si Sa Ket province wounded three Thai soldiers, with one losing a leg. The incident occurred while the soldiers were surveying the border. This blast marks a significant disruption to the relative calm established by the December 27 ceasefire following months of deadly clashes.
title: New landmine blast tests Thailand-Cambodia ceasefire

summary: Thailand's consumer confidence index rose to 52.8 in January from 51.9 in December. The University of the Thai Chamber of Commerce attributed this rise partly to the easing of border tensions with Cambodia and expectations surrounding the new government following the February general election.
title: Thailand's consumer confidence picks up in January

summary: The Cambodian government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, has filed a strong protest against the Thai military for actions in Banteay Meanchey province. Reports from local authorities indicate Thai forces destroyed civilian infrastructure and government buildings in the Boeung Trakuon area (Pillars 33-36) and conducted unauthorized road and ditch construction in Chouk Chey village (Pillars 46-47). Spokesperson Pen Bona stated these actions are a clear attempt to 'legitimize the unlawful occupation' of Cambodian land and violate the December 2025 ceasefire agreements.
title: Cambodia Protests New Actions by Thai Armed Forces

summary: General Romeo S. Brawner Jr., Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, met with PM Hun Manet in Phnom Penh. He reaffirmed that the Philippines, as the current ASEAN chair, is ready to lead the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) to ensure an impartial settlement of the border dispute. Hun Manet reiterated Cambodia's commitment to peaceful resolution based on international law.
title: The Philippines Ready to Continue Leading AOT to Facilitate Cambodia-Thailand Border Resolution

summary: Scholars from China, Cambodia, and Thailand met in Beijing on February 10 to advance the 'Fuxian consensus' reached in late 2025. The dialogue focused on restoring trust, which remains fragile due to legal disputes and nationalism. The experts proposed resuming bilateral exchanges and using the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation mechanism to stabilize the ceasefire.
title: Track II Diplomacy in Action: Scholars Forge Pathways for Cambodia-Thailand Peace

summary: International observers are pressuring both Thailand and Cambodia to uphold the fragile ceasefire as over 79,000 displaced residents remain unable to return home. Reports from Banteay Meanchey province indicate that Thai personnel have demolished some civilian infrastructure in the Boeng Trakuon area. The Cambodian government is urging the UN and ASEAN to monitor what it describes as continued 'military occupation' by Thai forces despite the halt in active fighting.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border remains under international scrutiny

summary: The Burapha Task Force apprehended 16 Chinese nationals (15 men, 1 woman) near Aranyaprathet on February 12 while they were illegally crossing from Poipet, Cambodia. The suspects were found with 226 mobile phones. They claimed to be administrators for online scam pages who were being forced to relocate to a third country by their employers but wished to return to China instead. They were handed over to local police for legal action.
title: 16 Chinese Nationals Arrested Fleeing Poipet at Thai-Border by Burapha Task Force

summary: Following the February 8 elections in Thailand, religious leaders are calling on the winning Bhumjaithai Party to prioritize a lasting peace deal. Reports indicate that the conflict has caused at least 18 civilian deaths in Cambodia and left 79 others injured as of late 2025.
title: Thai Bishop Calls on Newly Elected Government to Promote Lasting Peace with Cambodia

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) issued a statement categorically rejecting Cambodia's claims that Thailand has 'illegally occupied' or modified land in Banteay Meanchey. The MFA stated that Thai actions, including road construction and ditch-digging in the Ban Nong Chan (Sa Kaeo) area, are consistent with the December 27, 2025 Joint Statement. Cambodia had specifically protested infrastructure demolition in the Boeng Trakuon area, which Thailand denies.
title: MFA Rejects Allegations, Insists on Agreement Compliance after Cambodia Claims Illegal Occupation

summary: The government Information Center dismissed rumors of Thailand planning to 'zero' or cut diplomatic relations with Cambodia. It clarified that the recently approved budget for weaponry and border fencing is strictly for defensive purposes and to protect sovereignty, not as a provocation. The government emphasized using bilateral mechanisms like the JBC and RBC to resolve border disputes peacefully.
title: Information Center Refutes Rumors of Cutting Ties with Cambodia, Explains Budget for Weapons and Border Fences

summary: On February 13, the Pursat Provincial Administration clarified that Cambodian youths had been called in for guidance after cutting barbed wire installed by Thai forces in the Thma Da area. Authorities said they appreciated the youths' patriotic intent but warned the action could raise tensions. The administration said Cambodian and Thai officials had met on February 10 and that the Thai side had agreed to remove the wire itself.
title: Pursat Provincial Administration clarifies the case of calling Thma Da youths for instruction after acting in a disputed area with Thailand

summary: On February 13, Cambodian government spokesperson Pen Bona said foreign diplomatic missions, international organizations and major media were focusing on Cambodia's allegations of continued Thai military violations, including container placement, barbed wire and destruction of Cambodian infrastructure. He said Cambodia was pursuing formal protests and diplomacy to defend its sovereignty. The report did not describe a police-officer repatriation.
title: International community focuses on Thai military's continued violations of Cambodia

summary: The Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr., visited Banteay Meanchey province to assess the border situation. The Philippines is taking over leadership of the ASEAN Observers Team (AOT) from Malaysia. Prime Minister Hun Manet met with the General, reaffirming Cambodia's commitment to peaceful resolution based on historical Franco-Siamese treaties, while the government spokesperson highlighted ongoing Thai 'encroachments' in contested zones.
title: ASEAN Steps Up Mediation in Cambodia-Thailand Border Dispute as Philippines Takes Lead

summary: Cambodia's Ambassador to France, Luy David, reported to the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF) that Thai forces are still occupying Cambodian territory, building fences with shipping containers, and digging trenches. He stated that despite the December 27, 2025 ceasefire, Thailand continues to prevent 79,000 displaced Cambodians from returning home. The Ambassador urged the international community to monitor the situation, calling the Thai military presence 'unacceptable and inhumane.'
title: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Continued Border Violations Despite Ceasefire

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement rejecting Cambodia's 'unfounded allegations' regarding Thai activities along the border. Thailand maintains that its troop deployments and actions are fully consistent with the Joint Statement agreed upon during the ceasefire. The government also urged Cambodia to cooperate more effectively in suppressing online scam operations along the border through existing bilateral mechanisms.
title: Thailand rejects Cambodian allegations of border ceasefire violations

summary: Following a major election victory, acting PM Anutin Charnvirakul sent a stern message to Phnom Penh, declaring there will be 'no retreat, no dismantling of fences, and no opening of borders' in reclaimed areas. This signals a continuation of the high-pressure security policy on the border. Meanwhile, Cambodia has reportedly approached Vietnam to help mediate the dispute.
title: Acting PM Anutin Sets Hardline Stance: No Border Reopening, No Retreat

summary: Reports and viral video clips show Cambodian border troops active near the Preah Vihear area, Sisaket province. While Thai forces were operating cranes, Cambodian soldiers were filmed making provocative gestures and singing songs across the fence. Additionally, Cambodian military engineers are reportedly building new bunkers and fortifications despite the standing ceasefire agreement.
title: Cambodian Troops Still Active Near Border; Seen Taunting Thai Forces

summary: Deputy Prime Minister Hang Chuon Naron stated that the border conflict with Thailand has disrupted trade and production chains. He emphasized that the situation serves as a lesson for Cambodia to invest more in human capital and AI technology to ensure national resilience and long-term peace in a volatile global context.
title: Deputy PM Hang Chuon Naron: Border conflict with Thailand teaches us that only resilient human resources can protect social stability

summary: On February 13, Cambodian government spokesperson Pen Bona said Gen. Romeo S. Brawner Jr.'s four-day Cambodia visit was a formal precursor to the Philippines assuming AOT leadership from Malaysia. Brawner traveled to Banteay Meanchey to assess the border situation and receive AOT briefings, while the Philippines said it was prepared to lead the mission impartially.
title: ASEAN Steps Up Mediation in Cambodia-Thailand Border Dispute as Philippines Takes Lead

summary: The Thai-Cambodia Situation Information Center clarified that the Prime Minister's approval of the budget for weapon procurement and border fence construction is a routine security measure to protect sovereignty and prevent illegal activities. It denied rumors of cutting diplomatic ties but admitted to monitoring Cambodian movements, including potential military escalation or civilian protests.
title: Army on High Alert for Cambodian Provocations, Defends Border Fence Construction

summary: Khmer Times reported the Pursat Provincial Administration's February 13 clarification about youths who cut barbed wire installed by Thai forces in the Thma Da area. The administration said the youths were given guidance because unilateral action could increase tensions, and said a February 10 bilateral meeting had already produced an agreement for the Thai side to remove the wire itself.
title: ‘Patriotic’ youth given guidance after cutting barbed wire in disputed area of Cambodia-Thailand border

summary: Social activist Gun Jompluang posted video of a mission to place shipping containers as a border barrier at Ban Tha Sen, Trat. He claimed to have faced a large number of armed Cambodian soldiers who tried to block the installation. Thai Navy personnel and his bodyguards reportedly stood between him and the Cambodian troops to prevent a shootout during the mission.
title: Tense Standoff: Gun Jompluang Places Containers at Border, Confronts Armed Cambodian Troops

summary: Six weeks after the December 27 ceasefire, thousands of Cambodians remain in temporary shelters. Reuters reports that the Thai military has installed metal shipping containers and barbed wire at Ban Nong Ya Kaew (known as Prey Chan in Cambodia). While Thailand claims these barriers are for 'safety and security' consistent with the truce, Cambodian officials state 80% of homes in the area remain inaccessible. Recent landmine incidents continue to cause casualties, with a Thai soldier losing a leg on Feb 11.
title: Displaced Cambodians in limbo near contested border

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona announced that PM Hun Manet will lead a high-level delegation to Washington D.C. on Feb 19 for a peace council meeting. Additionally, the PM used social media to welcome cooperation with South Korea on fighting cross-border cybercrime, signaling a focus on digital security alongside traditional border issues.
title: Government Spokesperson Highlights Important Information Regarding Samdech Thipadei Hun Manet

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet visited over 1,000 displaced families at the Chan Sy Samaky Ratanaram Pagoda in Banteay Meanchey on Saturday. He reaffirmed the government's commitment to protecting citizens and preventing a return to armed conflict with Thailand, emphasizing that peace is the highest priority for the nation's development.
title: PM pledges to avert conflict while visiting displaced families

summary: Naewna reported a Royal Thai Navy statement that its humanitarian mine-action unit found six new-condition PMN-2 anti-personnel mines at Ban Chamrak, Trat, during operations on February 14. The Navy said its inspection concluded they had been newly placed by the opposing side rather than being older remnants, reported three PMN-1 mines and one POMZ mine nearby, and characterized the alleged placement as a serious violation of international humanitarian law and mine-ban obligations.
title: Thai Navy Finds New Cambodian Landmines in Trat, Denounces International Law Violation

summary: The Maritime Executive, citing Thai naval reporting, said groups of about 25 Cambodian fishing vessels entered waters off Koh Kut that Thailand treats as its territorial waters on February 9 and again on February 12; Thai patrol vessels escorted them out. The article also described a harder post-election Thai maritime posture, but did not report a formal suspension or termination of MOU 44.
title: New Thai Government Asserts Control over Coastal Waters

summary: Minister Keo Rattanak reported that the conflict has caused over $5 million in damage to electrical infrastructure and $6 million to educational facilities. The article highlights ongoing Cambodian protests against Thai military actions in Banteay Meanchey province.
title: Main National News for the Week 9-13/02/2026

summary: The Royal Government of Cambodia has formally escalated its diplomatic standoff, accusing Thailand of violating international law and both UN and ASEAN Charters. The accusation centers on the military occupation of disputed border territories. This follows months of tension and previous armed clashes in 2025.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Illegal Military Occupation in Border Row

summary: Khmer Times reported on February 16 that Philippine Armed Forces Chief Gen. Romeo S. Brawner Jr.'s Cambodia visit ran from February 11 to 14. It said that on Friday, February 13, he received an AOT briefing at CLG TS-2 at 10:00 and inspected the Boeung Trakuon border area at 14:05, later visiting Wat Kandol displacement camp. Cambodian officials used the visit to present their account of the border situation; territorial allegations in the report remain Cambodia's claims.
title: Philippine military chief visits border areas, displacement camps

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet visited 1,248 displaced families in Banteay Meanchey, pledging not to abandon them. The Ministry of Interior reports that 76,217 people remain displaced due to the conflict. The PM reiterated that Cambodia will not recognize boundary changes imposed by Thailand and remains committed to international law.
title: Displaced villagers heartened by PM's assurances of support

source: Asia News Network / The Phnom Penh Post
summary: Despite the closure of land borders following armed clashes, aviation officials report that 270 flights per week continue between Cambodia and Thailand. Ten airlines are maintaining operations, providing a vital economic and travel link while land crossings remain shuttered due to security concerns.
title: Cambodia–Thailand air corridor still open; 270 flights per week

summary: Army spokesperson Col. Winthai Suvaree confirmed forest fires on the Cambodian side opposite Preah Vihear and Chong Bok areas. While the fires do not threaten national security, there are concerns that the heat could trigger old landmines or unexploded ordnance (UXO) in the area. Army Region 2 is monitoring the situation closely and has instructed troops to operate with maximum caution.
title: Thai Army monitors forest fires on Cambodian border; cautions against unexploded ordnance

summary: Thai PBS reported on February 17 that Anutin Charnvirakul had posted on February 16 reaffirming Bhumjaithai's security platform, including continued border closures, construction of a security wall and cancellation of MOU 44. The article reviewed his February 6 campaign pledge and the February 10 Cabinet instruction to study lawful cancellation options; it did not report that MOU 44 had already been legally terminated.
title: Bhumjaithai Government vows to cancel MOU 2544 with Cambodia

summary: The Royal Thai Navy addressed reports that the Cambodian Navy seized a Thai vessel, 'Ko Chok Burapha,' near Koh Kong on February 14. Initial checks suggest the boat may have been sold to Cambodians previously, making the 'Thai seizure' label potentially inaccurate. Meanwhile, PM Anutin Charnvirakul is preparing a proposal for the Cabinet to ensure medical and support benefits for the families of soldiers killed during recent border duties.
title: Navy clarifies report of Cambodian seizure of Thai fishing boat; PM to seek benefits for border casualties

summary: The Secretary-General of the Council of State, Pakorn Nilprapunt, stated that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs must lead the study on canceling MOU 2544 regarding overlapping maritime areas. This follows an order from PM Anutin Charnvirakul. The legal move is seen as a push for national sovereignty after recent border clashes, though it requires careful consideration of international law.
title: Legal Council Studies Cancellation of MOU 2544 on Overlapping Claims

summary: The Philippines, as the 2026 ASEAN Chair, is facing its first major diplomatic test with the renewed frictions on the Cambodia-Thailand border. Analysts suggest that Manila will need to perform a delicate balancing act to maintain ASEAN centrality while navigating the involvement of major powers like the U.S. and China in the peace process.
title: Regional Flashpoints Set To Test Philippines Leadership As ASEAN Chair

summary: Speaking during his visit to the United States, PM Hun Manet stated that Thai forces are illegally occupying Cambodian land in multiple locations following clashes in 2025. He emphasized that Cambodia will never recognize border changes imposed by military force and called for the Joint Boundary Commission to resume work. He also highlighted Thai violations such as installing barbed wire and digging trenches in disputed areas.
title: Prime Minister Hun Manet: Cambodia will not accept illegal Thai occupation or forced border changes

source: Bangkok Biz News (กรุงเทพธุรกิจ)
summary: The Second Army Region reported several hotspots and wildfires in Cambodian territory near the Thai border, specifically near Chong Samet, Prasat Ta Muen, and Prasat Don Tual. Officials confirmed that the fires do not affect Thai military operations or security in the area but advised residents to follow official news to avoid misinformation.
title: Army Region 2 monitors border wildfires, confirms no impact on military readiness

summary: In a February 17 interview in Washington, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet told Reuters that Thai forces remained deep inside territory Cambodia considers its own after the December ceasefire. He said Thai troops had placed shipping containers and barbed wire on roads and that about 80,000 displaced Cambodians could not return home. Hun Manet urged an early resumption of Joint Boundary Commission technical work. Thailand denied occupying Cambodian territory, saying it was maintaining existing troop positions under the ceasefire and had not reinforced them.
title: Exclusive: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: During a visit to Washington for the 'Board of Peace' meeting, PM Hun Manet told Reuters that Thai forces are occupying territory deep within Cambodian lines, beyond Thailand's own unilateral claims. He cited the use of shipping containers and barbed wire to block roads. Thailand denies these claims, stating it is maintaining positions for de-escalation. Manet urged the Joint Boundary Commission to begin work now that Thailand's February 8 election is over.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: The analysis highlights that the border conflict has entered a dangerous phase where domestic political pressures in both Bangkok and Phnom Penh outweigh international mediation. Following the February 8 Thai general election, nationalist sentiments have risen. The report suggests that while a ceasefire is in place, military objectives in Bangkok and the vulnerabilities of Cambodia's forward defenses create a risk of a long-term contest rather than a permanent peace.
title: Thailand-Cambodia conflict: The trap of a long war

source: PRD Thailand / Ministry of Foreign Affairs
summary: PRD Thailand relayed the February 18 Foreign Ministry briefing that the border was relatively calm and that three formal Regional Border Committee meetings in the previous two months had not yet reached consensus on area management. The ministry characterized the meetings as a positive development, said direct communication channels remained active, and said negotiations would continue.
title: Border Situation Relatively Calm but RBC Meetings End Without Consensus

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs is closely watching Cambodian PM Hun Manet's attempts to raise the border dispute on international platforms. Thailand is prepared to counter any 'distorted information' regarding territorial violations. The ministry also noted that the official cancellation of MOU 44 must wait for the formation of the new Thai government following the recent elections.
title: Foreign Ministry Monitors Hun Manet's International Moves on Border Dispute

summary: VOD reported that on February 17, Thai Second Army Region commander Lt Gen Weerayut Raksin ordered troops to be ready to push back or respond immediately if Cambodian forces again obstructed Thai canal-digging or barbed-wire work. VOD said Cambodian troops had challenged canal work in Chouk Chey on February 16 and that Thai forces continued ditch work at Jam Tae near Ta Mok on February 17. Weerayut maintained that the work was in Thai territory under Thailand's 1:50,000 map; Cambodian sources disputed the boundary and described the work as encroachment.
title: Thai military chief threatens Cambodia not to block new border canals encroaching on Cambodian land

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Thai forces are illegally occupying Cambodian territory despite a peace agreement mediated by U.S. President Donald Trump. He noted that Thai troops remain in multiple locations beyond even Thailand's own claim lines and are attempting to create 'new facts on the ground' by installing barbed wire, shipping containers, and digging trenches. He reaffirmed that Cambodia will never recognize any border modifications imposed through force.
title: PM says Cambodia will not accept illegal Thai occupation or forced border changes

summary: Analysts warn that the border dispute with Thailand is unlikely to be resolved soon, citing nationalist rhetoric in Thai politics following the victory of the Bhumjaithai Party. Dr. Chey Tech suggested that Cambodia should strengthen its diplomatic position through ASEAN and international observers, compiling evidence of infrastructure construction in disputed areas to build legal support. He emphasized that the border issue is often used for domestic political gain in Thailand.
title: Cambodia Must Prepare for Long-Term Border Tensions, Analysts Say

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet told Reuters that Thai forces are occupying Cambodian land despite the ceasefire agreement brokered by US President Donald Trump at the end of 2025. He emphasized that Cambodia will not accept illegal occupation or forced changes to its borders. The PM expressed hope that the newly formed Board of Peace could help ease these 'fragile' tensions, while noting that Thai troops have destroyed civilian homes in areas they seized during the incursions last year.
title: Samdech Thipadei tells Reuters Thailand is occupying Cambodian territory after ceasefire

summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) stated that the border has been mostly peaceful for two months following the Trump-brokered Kuala Lumpur Peace Declaration. However, Thailand expressed concern over Cambodia's continued 'provocations' and the spreading of false information in international forums, alleging Thai occupation of Cambodian land.
title: MFA briefs on 6 key border developments, urges Cambodia to stop 'misinformation'

summary: The Thai Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) meetings will proceed once the new Thai cabinet is settled after the February 8 elections. Thailand officially expressed concern over 'distorted' claims by PM Hun Manet to international media regarding illegal occupation, asserting that Thailand is strictly following the December 27 ceasefire agreement.
title: Thai-Cambodia JBC to Resume After New Gov Formed; Thailand Urges End to Distorted News

summary: Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet has accused Thailand of maintaining military positions deep within Cambodian territory despite the December 27 ceasefire. Speaking from Washington, he described the border situation as 'fragile' and called for the resumption of the Joint Boundary Commission. He suggested that U.S. President Donald Trump's new 'Board of Peace' could assist in de-escalation.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand occupying 'deep' territory after ceasefire

summary: The Nation reported on February 19 that Thailand's Second Army Region said Cambodian forces had made significant movements in the Hill 745 area near Ubon Ratchathani on February 16, with the Thai military estimating nearly 10,000 Cambodian soldiers in the sector. The troop figure and movement assessment are attributed to Thai military reporting; the article also discussed Thailand's planned diplomatic messaging on Cambodia-based online scams at the UN Human Rights Council.
title: Thailand and Cambodia's diplomatic rivalry intensifies as online scams add complexity to border tensions

summary: Reports indicate that Thai soldiers and media recently visited areas near Sadok Kok Thom Historical Park as tensions remain high. PM Hun Manet alleged that Thailand's recent election, which saw the victory of PM Anutin Charnvirakul, involved 'heightened nationalist rhetoric' that has delayed technical boundary work.
title: Thailand still 'occupying' territory after ceasefire, Cambodia PM says

summary: The Royal Thai Army spokesperson, Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, rejected accusations made by Hun Manet. Thailand claims the area in question is Thai territory where Cambodian civilians and soldiers encroached over time after being sheltered during past wars. The spokesperson stated these individuals are not 'displaced persons' but are violating Thai sovereignty, and the use of barriers is a lawful measure to secure Thai territory.
title: Thailand rejects Cambodian PM's border occupation claims

summary: Local reports from Buriram province describe intentional forest fires near the Chong Sai Taku border crossing, allegedly started by Cambodian soldiers. These 'fire rain' sparks are blowing into Thai villages, causing panic among residents who fear the ceasefire might collapse. Local officials have put emergency teams on 24-hour standby and are preparing evacuation plans if the situation escalates.
title: Tensions Rise in Buriram: Cambodian Troops Accused of Starting Fires to Provoke Thai Forces

summary: Thai Army spokesperson Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree dismissed accusations made by Cambodian PM Hun Manet in a Reuters interview. The Army claims that the installation of containers and barbed wire are temporary security measures to prevent confrontations, and that Thailand is operating within its own territory according to the December ceasefire agreement. Winthai alleged that Cambodian civilians have been used to provoke Thai forces in the past.
title: Thai Army Rejects Cambodian PM’s Claims of Border Occupation

summary: In an exclusive interview with Reuters while visiting Washington D.C., Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Thai forces are occupying territory 'deep' into Cambodia, beyond even Thailand's own claims. He described the situation as 'fragile' and called for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to resume work. Thailand's Ministry of Defense denied the claims, stating they are adhering to the joint agreement to maintain existing troop deployments without further reinforcement.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: Reporting from Washington, Hun Manet urged Thailand to allow the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to begin demarcation immediately. He noted that technical work has been delayed, with Thailand citing its February 8, 2026, election as a reason for postponement. The Cambodian leader stressed that while ties with the US and China are strong, the border remains a critical flashpoint that requires international attention through the newly formed 'Board of Peace'.
title: Cambodia alleges Thailand violating territorial agreement

summary: The ongoing border tension between Cambodia and Thailand has caused a severe economic slump in Thailand's Aranyaprathet district. Local markets, including Rong Kluea Market, have seen many shops close due to the border remaining shut since mid-2025. Local residents express concern over financial strain and fear a third round of border clashes.
title: Border dispute causes Aranyaprathet's economy to decline sharply

summary: An extraordinary committee from the Senate visited the border areas in Sisaket province to evaluate the pros and cons of canceling the MOUs signed in 2000 and 2001. This follows growing domestic pressure and political promises to scrap the agreements amidst the ongoing maritime and land border disputes.
title: Senate Committee visits Sisaket border to study MOU 2000/2001 cancellation

summary: An investigative report claims that the conflict has resulted in approximately 149 deaths and displaced 640,000 civilians. The report criticizes Thailand for rejecting multiple mediation offers from the U.S., China, and Malaysia, and alleges the use of disproportionate force, including cluster munitions in late 2025. It also highlights the link between border tensions and the crackdown on Cambodian-based scam centers.
title: How Thailand Turned a Border Dispute Into an Illegal War

summary: DAP News reproduced a Cambodian Ministry of Interior update covering 06:00 on February 18 to 06:00 on February 19. The ministry said 1,434 more displaced people returned during the period; nearly 580,000, or 89%, of more than 640,000 had returned overall; and 70,516 remained unable to return, including 37,165 women and 24,924 children. The ministry separately repeated Cambodian allegations about Thai military barriers and recent infrastructure activity in Banteay Meanchey.
title: Ministry of Interior: 1,434 more displaced persons return home

summary: The Thai Situation Center issued a clarification regarding 'inaccurate' international media reports. It denied claims that Thailand's military response was disproportionate, explaining that the use of F-16 aircraft was a necessary self-defense measure under UN Charter Article 51. The center claimed Cambodian forces initiated attacks on Thai military and civilian areas first, and the Thai airstrikes strictly targeted military positions to protect citizens.
title: Thai Situation Center Rebuts Foreign Media Claims Over F-16 Usage

summary: Recent developments highlight a shift in Cambodian diplomacy, using the 'Board of Peace' meeting to spotlight the Thai military occupation. Cambodia is reportedly planning to build 3,000 houses for displaced residents near the border, while analysts warn that ongoing conflicts and regional sanctions make ambitious trade targets between the two nations unrealistic for the 2026 fiscal year.
title: Asia Daily: February 19, 2026

summary: Fresh News reported Japan's US$1 million grant to the International Labour Organization for vocational skills training, re-employment assistance and livelihood recovery for Cambodian workers returning from Thailand due to the border conflict. The project covers Preah Vihear, Oddar Meanchey and Pursat provinces.
title: Japan Provides $1M for Promoting Employment of Returning Migrant Workers Affected by the Border Conflict

summary: U.S. Deputy Secretary Landau met with PM Hun Manet in Washington to discuss the Cambodia-Thailand border situation. The U.S. commended Cambodia's participation as a founding member of the Board of Peace. The discussions also covered security cooperation and efforts to combat international online scam operations targeting Americans, which has become a secondary point of friction in the border dispute.
title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet

summary: Tourism operators in seven provinces along the Thailand-Cambodia border are appealing for government stimulus. Despite the current ceasefire, domestic and international tourism has plummeted since mid-2025 due to the conflict, leaving businesses in Ubon Ratchathani, Sisaket, and Sa Kaeo struggling.
title: Thai-Cambodian border provinces seek tourism recovery measures

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet stated that Thai forces remain inside Cambodian territory beyond the boundary lines claimed by Bangkok, causing significant hardship for local communities. Speaking from the United States while attending a 'Board of Peace' meeting, he called for the Joint Boundary Commission (JBC) to urgently resume technical work. He noted that despite the Dec 27 ceasefire, Thai troops have placed shipping containers and barbed wire across roads, preventing villagers from accessing their lands.
title: Hun Manet urges swift border demarcation as Thai Troops remain in Cambodian territory

summary: The Thai Navy arrested 5 Chinese nationals and 1 Cambodian fleeing into Chanthaburi from Cambodia. They were found with 270 mobile phones and numerous SIM cards. The Navy spokesperson criticized Cambodia, stating the escape reflects a 'structural failure' of the neighboring state to prevent its territory from being used as a base for international cybercrime (Cyber Scams).
title: Thai Navy Arrests Cyber Scam Gang Fleeing Cambodia with 270 Phones

summary: Thai officials have formally rejected claims by Cambodian PM Hun Manet that Thailand is occupying territory beyond agreed zones. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow is preparing to clarify facts regarding the border situation and the regional scammer crisis at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva later this month. Military communication channels remain active despite the verbal sparring.
title: Thailand Rebuts Hun Manet’s Border Claims

summary: Tensions remain high as the Thai Army Region 2 monitors movement of nearly 10,000 Cambodian troops near Chong Bok. Diplomatically, Thailand is using the issue of Cambodia-based online scam centers to counter Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet's international lobbying regarding border disputes. Meanwhile, the Thai Foreign Ministry is gathering historical documents from France to prepare for technical border talks.
title: Thai-Cambodia Border Diplomacy: 'Online Scams' Pressure Hun Manet

summary: The 2nd Army Region reported 8 wildfire surveillance points along the border. While smoke and fires were observed on the Cambodian side near the Thai border, the situation is currently under control. Military units are monitoring the situation closely to prevent the fire from spreading into Thai territory, particularly in Ubon Ratchathani and Surin.
title: 2nd Army Region Monitors 8 Wildfire Spots Along Thai-Cambodia Border

source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
summary: Japan's Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation, Hayashi Teiji, is scheduled to visit Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines (ASEAN Chair) from February 23 to 27. The mission aims to encourage the steady implementation of the December 27 ceasefire. Japan has already provided equipment to the ASEAN Observer Team (AOT) and is engaging in diplomatic efforts to ensure regional stability amid the fragile border situation.
title: Visit of Ambassador for Mekong Cooperation HAYASHI to Thailand, Cambodia, and the Philippines

summary: The Royal Thai Army has responded to allegations from Cambodian PM Hun Manet, insisting that the disputed areas belong to Thailand. Military officials criticized the lack of discipline among Cambodian troops newly deployed to the area and stated that Thai forces are prepared and disciplined in their defense of the frontier. The Army is coordinating with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to officially counter Cambodia's narrative.
title: Thai Army Slams Cambodia, Reaffirms Territory as Thai

summary: Thai media reports that Cambodian soldiers allegedly started forest fires along the border to harass Thai troops. However, strong winds blew the flames back into Cambodia, destroying a wood processing factory belonging to a deputy district chief and over 60 civilian homes in Battambang and Preah Vihear provinces. Thai forces remain on high alert due to the smoke and proximity of the fires to Thai military bases.
title: Cambodian Soldiers' Border Fire Backfires, Burns Own Villages

summary: The Royal Thai Navy's First Fleet intercepted an unregistered Cambodian wooden boat in the eastern sea border. The vessel was found smuggling a large quantity of seafood to be transferred to Thai fishing boats to avoid customs. Three Cambodian crew members were arrested and sent to Khlong Yai Police Station for legal action.
title: Navy Seizes Cambodian Vessel Smuggling Seafood to Thai Boats

summary: Thai media reports on Cambodian PM Hun Manet's interview with Fox News Digital, where he alleged Thai military advancement into overlapping claim areas has displaced over 80,000 Cambodians. The Thai military has not yet issued a formal counter-statement to these specific international allegations, though the tone in Thai media remains skeptical of the '80,000' figure.
title: Hun Manet complains to Fox News about Thai 'encroachment' affecting 80,000 displaced people

summary: Khmer Times reported Prime Minister Hun Manet's allegation that Thai forces were occupying areas Cambodia considers its territory and using unilateral maps, trenches and barriers that obstructed some residents' return. The article repeated the roughly 80,000-person displacement figure. It establishes Cambodia's claim and the reported displacement, not independent proof that Thai fortifications were the sole cause preventing all 80,000 people from returning.
title: Border map dispute nixes displaced people's return

summary: In a February 17 interview in Washington, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet told Reuters that Thai forces remained inside territory Cambodia considers its own after the December ceasefire. He said Thai troops had placed shipping containers and barbed wire on roads and that displaced residents could not return home. Thailand denied occupying Cambodian territory, saying it was maintaining existing troop positions under the ceasefire and had not reinforced them.
title: Cambodian PM says Thailand is occupying territory after Trump-brokered ceasefire

summary: AKP reported Cambodia Ministry of Interior figures on February 12 saying about 80,000 of more than 640,000 displaced people remained in camps. The ministry said those still unable to return faced multiple causes, including heavily damaged homes, unexploded ordnance, and alleged Thai destruction or road blockages using barbed wire, containers, and other obstacles.
title: Some 80,000 Displaced People Remain in Camps

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that the border tension has reached the highest level of global discourse after US President Donald Trump referenced the 'nasty war' between the two nations during his speech on Feb 19. Cambodia alleges that Thai occupation and restrictions are preventing over 70,000 displaced Cambodians from returning to their homes.
title: Cambodia-Thailand border spat gains global attention at Board of Peace meeting

summary: Spokesperson Pen Bona expressed hope that PM Hun Manet's diplomatic mission in Washington will help restore stability. The government maintains that Thai troops are currently occupying several areas inside Cambodia’s sovereign borders. Analysts suggest that engaging global media like Reuters and Fox News is a strategic move to expose Thailand's perceived 'aggression'.
title: Cambodia says border dispute with Thailand will be restored after Hun Manet's presence at Peace Council meeting

summary: The Thailand-Cambodia Border Defense Command reported seven fire or hotspot locations on February 20: one south of Chong An Ma on the Cambodian side, three in Cambodian areas opposite Si Sa Ket and three in Cambodian areas opposite Surin. The closest listed sites were about 500 metres from the Thai border. The command attributed most fires to burning for agriculture or housing preparation, hunting and forest-product gathering, while saying Thai forces continued patrols, observation posts and base-security measures.
title: Border Forces report 7 major forest fires near Thai-Cambodian border

summary: In Washington D.C., PM Hun Manet met with Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan. The meeting touched upon the roots of the Cambodia-Thailand border conflict. Hun Manet briefed the Turkish diplomat on recent developments and reaffirmed Cambodia's stance on resolving the dispute peacefully based on international law. The Turkish Foreign Minister expressed interest in the issue and hoped for long-term peace between the two neighbors.
title: Turkish Foreign Minister hopes Cambodia-Thailand can achieve permanent peace in the future

summary: On February 19 in Washington, Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet met U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau during his Board of Peace visit. Cambodian reporting said Landau thanked Cambodia for joining as a founding member of the Board of Peace, highlighted U.S. support for lasting peace along the Cambodia-Thailand border, and discussed the growing U.S.-Cambodia partnership. Hun Manet briefed the U.S. side on the border situation and Cambodia's peaceful position under international law.
title: US Deputy Secretary of State Reaffirms Support for Lasting Peace along Cambodia–Thailand Border

summary: During a meeting with CPP officials in Svay Rieng, Samdech Men Sam An briefed members on the border developments. She stated that the government is working hard to prevent the border situation with Thailand from escalating into a more serious conflict. The meeting aimed to update local officials on the political situation so they can manage public sentiment and maintain peace and stability at the grassroots level.
title: Cambodian leaders strive to manage situation, avoid serious problems

summary: The Royal Thai Armed Forces have officially released a white paper containing maps and historical evidence to justify Thai troop positions. This moves the conflict into a legal and diplomatic documentation phase, aiming to rebut PM Hun Manet's claims of 'nasty war' and territorial theft presented during his recent visit to the U.S.
title: Thai Armed Forces release 'White Paper' to counter Cambodian border claims

summary: PPTV reported Thailand's 2nd Army Region statement denying that Thai units used firearms against Cambodian personnel in the Chong An Ma area. The statement said Thai units exercised restraint, followed rules on the use of force, were prepared to coordinate transparent joint fact-finding, and warned that inaccurate information could affect bilateral relations and border calm.
title: Army Region 2 Denies Firing at Cambodian Personnel in Chong An Ma Area

summary: Atlantic Council CEO Frederick Kempe met PM Hun Manet in Washington to discuss the roots of the border dispute. Hun Manet emphasized that Thai forces are currently occupying locations deep inside Cambodian territory, which he claimed is a factual reality on the ground, not an unfounded accusation. He requested the Council to help share the truth of the conflict with the global community.
title: Atlantic Council CEO wants to learn more about Cambodia-Thailand border conflict

summary: A report citing a 'New York Editorial' claims Thailand's actions violate international law. It alleges Thai forces used cluster bombs and air strikes deep in Cambodian territory, causing 149 deaths and displacing 640,000 civilians. The report characterizes Thailand's 'online scam' accusations as a pretext for invasion and illegal blockades of fuel and sea routes.
title: American media 'unmasks Thailand', showing the world the transformation of border dispute into illegal war

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally protested the February 22 detention of three Cambodian nationals and seizure of their fishing boat. Cambodia said the incident occurred about 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor in Koh Kong province within Cambodian territorial waters, demanded the crew and vessel be released, and called for an end to what it described as unauthorised Thai naval patrols and law-enforcement activity.
title: The Royal Government of Cambodia formally protests the unauthorized presence of Royal Thai Navy vessels

summary: Cambodia has filed a formal protest against the Royal Thai Navy for alleged unauthorized presence in its territorial waters off Koh Kong. The incident involved the arrest of three Cambodians and the seizure of their fishing vessel approximately 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor. Cambodia labels this a 'clear violation' of international law and sovereignty.
title: Thai Navy Breached Cambodia's Sovereign Waters, Conducted Unauthorised Patrols

summary: Royal Government Spokesperson Pen Bona formally accused Thai military forces of a territorial incursion, alleging they remain positioned deep inside Cambodian territory. The spokesperson claimed Thai troops are using barbed wire and shipping containers to block nearly 80,000 displaced Cambodian civilians from returning home. Phnom Penh reiterated its rejection of military force to alter borders and urged Thailand to allow the Joint Border Commission to resume work following the conclusion of Thailand's elections.
title: Cambodia accuses Thailand of incursion, calls for de-escalation amid diplomatic push

summary: Reports suggest a possible 'setup' by Cambodian forces after they claimed a soldier was wounded by Thai fire at Chong An Ma. Thai security sources argue the wound appears inconsistent with a bullet strike, possibly being a scratch or cut instead. The report emphasizes adhering to the ceasefire and GBC agreements despite these accusations.
title: Cambodia Staging Incident? Experts Spot Irregularities in Soldier's Wounds After Shooting Claim

summary: Two Cambodian journalists, Phorn Sopheap and Pheap Pheara, are appealing their 14-year prison sentences for treason. They were convicted in December 2025 for posting Facebook photos of border clashes with Thailand, which allegedly included images of land mines. International rights groups have condemned the sentences as a suppression of press freedom.
title: 2 Cambodian journalists appeal treason convictions over a photo from Thai border clash

summary: A February 22 report citing Thai security officials said the Cambodian side had reported that at about 10:45 on February 20, 5–7 gunshots were heard at Chong An Ma and one Cambodian soldier was found with a knee injury that Cambodia attributed to fire from the Thai side. Thai security sources questioned whether the photographed injury matched forensic gunshot patterns and called for a full forensic examination before conclusions.
title: Cambodian Soldier Claims Shot at 'Chong An Ma'; Thai Security Says Wounds Don't Match Gunfire

summary: The Second Army Region reported that wildfires are still active at three locations near Khao Satta Som and Don Tual Castle, originating from the Cambodian side. The fires are suspected to be caused by agricultural burning or hunting. Thai security forces are patrolling and creating firebreaks to prevent the fire from crossing the border, while the situation at Khao Phra Viharn (Pha Mo I Daeng) remains normal.
title: Wildfires continue at 3 spots along Thai-Cambodian border in Si Sa Ket

summary: The Nation reported the Royal Thai Navy's response to Cambodia's protest. The Navy said patrol craft T.996 detected, searched and detained the boat at 09:30 on February 22, cited coordinates 11°32.63' N, 102°50.54' E, and said the location was about two nautical miles inside Thai waters. Three Cambodian crew members were detained; the sovereignty and location claims remain Thailand's account.
title: Navy confirms Cambodian fishing boat seized in Thai waters

summary: Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree, Army spokesperson, addressed allegations from a foreign page ('The New York Editorial') claiming Thailand used disproportionate force. He clarified that F-16s were used only against military targets after Cambodia fired heavy weapons first. He denied the use of cluster munitions against people, stating that DPICM was used on equipment, and claimed the death of a Cambodian child was due to old explosives, not Thai actions.
title: Army rebuts seven fake news claims on Thai-Cambodia border

summary: The Royal Thai Army has rejected an international report claiming Thailand used excessive force, including F-16 airstrikes, to influence domestic elections in Bangkok. Army spokesperson Maj Gen Winthai Suvaree stated that operations are strictly 'legitimate self-defence' under the UN Charter and denied using the border dispute for political gain.
title: Thai army insists Cambodia border actions not politically motivated

summary: During his visit to Washington D.C., PM Hun Manet informed leaders from the UN, Hungary, Indonesia, and Vietnam about the 'real situation' where Thai forces have allegedly invaded and occupied Cambodian territory. He called for the full implementation of existing agreements and the safe return of civilians to their homes, stressing that peace remains Cambodia's core value.
title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: PM Hun Manet informs counterparts about real situation on border

summary: During the Inaugural Meeting of the Board of Peace in Washington, D.C., PM Hun Manet briefed international counterparts and media on the border conflict. He called for the full implementation of existing agreements, a peaceful settlement according to international law, and the safe return of Cambodian civilians to their homes.
title: PM Hun Manet Briefs All Counterparts on Cambodia-Thailand Border Situation, Reaffirms Peace as Core Value

summary: Prime Minister Hun Manet attended the inaugural Board of Peace meeting in Washington, DC, where he described the current ceasefire with Thailand as 'fragile.' He highlighted the ongoing tensions to world leaders, seeking international attention to the border dispute that saw major clashes in late 2025. He emphasized Cambodia's commitment to peace but noted that the situation remains unstable despite the US-brokered agreement.
title: Hun Manet calls attention to ‘fragile’ ceasefire at meeting of world leaders in US

summary: Government spokesperson Pen Bona stated that Cambodia remains committed to the ceasefire agreement reached in late 2025 despite the ongoing territorial disputes and presence of Thai troops in disputed zones. He emphasized that the Cambodian leadership's priority is maintaining peace and adhering to international law.
title: Pen Bona: In the spirit of loving peace, Cambodia continues to respect the ceasefire

summary: While Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow accused Cambodia of provoking tensions, Cambodian media highlights shipping containers set up by Thai soldiers in Chouk Chey village, Banteay Meanchey. The Cambodian government is using international platforms to report what it describes as Thai infringements on sovereignty, countering Thai claims that the issue should only be handled bilaterally without third-party involvement.
title: Cambodia tells its side of the story on world stage

summary: Thai Defence Minister Nattaphon Nakpanich said the ministry proposed a gradual troop reduction along the 798km Thai-Cambodian border to reduce costs while retaining forces where still needed. He said populated border areas such as Khlong Luek and opposite Thmor Da should have stronger fencing and electronic monitoring, and proposed veteran villages to help watch the border. He separately said Chong An Ma, Chong Bok and Phu Makua could eventually be developed as tourist attractions.
title: Thailand proposes troop cutback along Cambodian border to reduce costs

summary: Lieutenant General Maly Socheata categorically denied Thai military reports that Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol near Preah Vihear on Feb 24. She stated that Cambodian forces heard explosions on the Thai side but did not fire any weapons, urging Thailand to stop spreading 'fake news' that increases border tensions.
title: Press Release of Lt. Gen. Maly Socheata, Spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence

summary: Cambodian Ambassador to France, Luy David, addressed the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF), stating that 60,000 displaced Cambodians, including many women and girls, are unable to return home due to Thai military infrastructure like shipping containers and barbed wire on 'sovereign Cambodian land.' The report emphasizes the humanitarian impact of the ongoing border tension.
title: Ambassador to France Briefs OIF on Vulnerability of Cambodian Women Amid Thai Invasion

summary: An analysis of Thailand's observer status at Donald Trump's inaugural 'Board of Peace' (BOP) meeting in Washington. While Cambodia is a founding member, Thai media were concerned about the Thai flag appearing in the background. The incoming Thai government is weighing the implications of joining the BOP, especially given Hun Manet's active praise of Trump and his nomination of Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize, which could complicate existing border tensions.
title: The fuss about Thailand and the BOP

summary: Naewna reported that on February 23 Thai Defence Minister Gen Nattaphon Nakpanich said he had complained to Cambodian Defence Minister Tea Seiha that Cambodian soldiers were setting fires along the border and called them undisciplined. He separately said some busy border areas, including Ban Khlong Luek and Thmor Da, might need permanent and electronic fencing with CCTV. The arson claim is the Thai minister's allegation, and the report does not establish the fencing discussion as a direct response to a specific fire.
title: 'Big Lek' Blasts Cambodia: Slams Undisciplined Soldiers for Setting Forest Fires to Harass Thai Border

summary: Thai military units reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in the Phan Hin Paed Kon area of Sisaket province. The incident reportedly began when Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade (M79) at a Thai patrol, prompting Thai soldiers to return fire. No Thai casualties were reported, and the situation has since calmed, though troops remain on high alert. The Thai military suggests the incident may have been caused by a lack of coordination during a Cambodian troop rotation.
title: Border Tensions! Thai and Cambodian Troops Clash at Phan Hin Paed Kon

summary: Civil society organizations released a statement noting that 170,000 civilians remain displaced and unable to return home due to military presence and infrastructure damage. The report highlights incursions in Cambodian territory and the destruction of civilian assets, urging both nations to honor the ASEAN Charter and previous ceasefire commitments.
title: Statement Calling for Legal and Peaceful Resolution of the Cambodia–Thailand Border Conflict

summary: Ambassador Luy David reported to the Francophonie Governance Council that over 60,000 Cambodians, including many women and children, cannot return home because Thai troops have placed shipping containers and barbed wire in occupied areas. He stated that 32 people died and 95 were injured during the 21-day 'invasion war' in December 2025. Currently, 35,099 women remain in temporary safety camps as of February 23, 2026, due to Thai military obstructions and unexploded ordnance.
title: Cambodian Ambassador highlights pain of Cambodian women due to Thai invasion at Governance Council meeting

summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow stated that Cambodia's leadership continues to use 'old tactics' of fabricating news to pressure Thailand on the global stage. He revealed that he recently met with UNESCO's Director-General to clarify that Thailand did not intend to damage the Preah Vihear Temple, blaming the damage on Cambodia using the site as a military base and weapons cache. Thailand maintains a stance of restraint while seeking to rebuild mutual trust.
title: Sihasak Claims Cambodian Leader Still Fabricating Stories to Discredit Thailand Internationally

summary: Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow rejected claims by Cambodian PM Hun Manet that Thai forces are occupying Cambodian territory. Sihasak stated that both nations agreed to a ceasefire where troops stay in current positions, though he described the peace as 'fragile.' He accused Cambodia of 'internationalising' the conflict to stir sentiment.
title: Thai FM hits back at Cambodia's 'occupation' claim in France 24 interview

summary: The Ministry of National Defence officially rejected Thai media reports claiming Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol in Preah Vihear on Feb 24. Spokesperson Maly Socheata stated that RCAF troops heard explosions from the Thai side first and contacted Thai counterparts to clarify that no Cambodian weapons were fired.
title: Cambodia denies Thai claims of grenade launcher fire near Preah Vihear border

summary: Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow delivered a statement at the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva, rejecting Cambodia's accusations of territorial encroachment. He described Cambodia's narrative as distorted and 'demonizing' Thailand. Sihasak emphasized that Thailand remains committed to the December ceasefire and peaceful diplomacy but blamed the recent friction on Cambodian provocations and interference in Thai internal politics.
title: FM Counters Cambodia’s Border Remarks, Reaffirms Thailand’s Stance

summary: The Thai army reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. According to the Thai statement, Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol, prompting a return shot from an M79 launcher as a warning. No injuries were reported. The Thai military suggested the incident might have been caused by a rotation of new Cambodian troops unfamiliar with the area.
title: Thai army says exchanged fire with Cambodia at border

summary: The Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (DE) issued a warning about viral fake news claiming Cambodia has deployed PHL-03 long-range rocket launchers near the border, targeting Nakhon Ratchasima. The ministry clarified that this is false information intended to cause public panic during the ongoing border tensions and urged citizens to follow only official government updates.
title: DE Warns of Fake News Regarding Cambodian Missile Deployment

summary: Cambodia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a formal protest after the Royal Thai Navy arrested three Cambodian fishermen and seized their boat 7.2 nautical miles from Koh Yor Island in Koh Kong province. Officials called the act a 'clear violation of sovereignty.' While land borders are quiet, maritime tensions remain high following the 2025 conflict.
title: Cambodia protests Thai navy presence in its waters

summary: On the morning of February 24, 2026, a 40mm grenade was fired from the Cambodian side at a Thai patrol in Si Sa Ket's Kantharalak district. Thai forces responded with an M79 warning shot. The Thai military believes the incident was caused by newly rotated Cambodian troops unfamiliar with the area. No injuries were reported, and the Army Chief has ruled out further escalation.
title: Thailand blames Cambodia after brief border exchange

summary: Cambodia's Information Minister Neth Pheaktra dismissed Thai military claims that Cambodian soldiers fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol in Sisaket province. Thailand's army reported returning fire as a warning, suggesting the incident might have been caused by new, inexperienced Cambodian troops during a rotation. Cambodia labeled the claims as 'fabricated' and intended to mislead public opinion.
title: Cambodia rejects claim its forces fired on Thai patrol

summary: Tensions remain high following a reported skirmish in the Sisaket province. While the Thai military accused Cambodia of violating the December ceasefire by firing a grenade, Phnom Penh officials have denied the use of any weapons. This flare-up is the first significant incident since the December 2025 truce, following a year of conflict that displaced over a million people.
title: Thailand, Cambodia dispute exchange of fire at border

summary: Maly Socheata, spokesperson for the Ministry of National Defence, strongly denied claims by the Thai military that Cambodian soldiers fired a 40mm grenade near a Thai patrol on February 24. She called the reports 'false and fabricated,' aimed at misleading the public. Military Region 4 confirmed that while explosions were heard on the Thai side, Cambodian forces were not involved.
title: Cambodia Rejects Thai Accusations of 40mm Grenade Fire

summary: The Second Army Region reported that on February 24, Cambodian forces fired a 40mm grenade at a Thai patrol near Phlan Hin Paed Kon in Si Sa Ket province. The grenade landed near the cliff edge about 2km from the base. Thai forces returned fire according to engagement rules. No Thai casualties or damage were reported, and the situation is currently under control.
title: Second Army Region confirms Thailand safe after Cambodia opened fire; Thai forces returned warning shots

summary: Thailand's military reported an exchange of fire with Cambodian forces in Sisaket province on Tuesday morning. The Thai army claims Cambodian troops fired a 40mm grenade, prompting a warning shot in return. Cambodia's Ministry of Information denied the claims, calling them 'fabricated'. The incident threatens the December truce that ended months of heavy fighting which displaced over a million people in 2025.
title: Thailand says troops exchanged fire at border, Cambodia denies ceasefire breach

summary: Cambodian Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Prak Sokhonn alleged on the international stage that Thailand has established military bases within Cambodian territory. He claimed this aggression has forced over 650,000 Cambodian civilians to evacuate. This statement was met with a swift counter-rebuttal from the Thai Foreign Ministry later that day.
title: Cambodia Accuses Thailand of Building Bases on Its Territory, 650,000 Displaced

summary: Following a massive explosion at a Thai Border Patrol Police ammunition depot in Surin province on Tuesday night, Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul clarified the incident was a technical accident caused by heat, not an attack or related to border tensions. The fire destroyed small arms ammunition, mortars, and grenades, leading to the evacuation of 300 residents. Cambodian media reported this to allay local fears of renewed border fighting.
title: Anutin clarifies that the Surin ammo warehouse fire is not related to the Cambodia-Thailand border issue

summary: A coalition of 424 Cambodian civil society organizations issued a joint statement condemning Thai military movements. They allege that Thai troops destroyed civilian homes, schools, and health centers in contested areas. The groups claim Thai airstrikes and rockets previously reached 36km inside Cambodia, and they are now calling for international accountability for the displacement of civilians.
title: Thailand accused of breaching UN, ASEAN commitments

They demand a transparent historical verification of shared or overlapping cultures.

title: Second Army Region Explains Measures to Control Fuel Oil Exports to Laos with Added GPS Tracking
summary: Thai Rath reported that on February 28 the Second Army Region Operations Center explained a controlled framework for fuel exports to Laos after the earlier suspension. The Army said controls included GPS tracking from origin to destination, officer checks of fuel type, volume and vehicles, certification of unloading at authorised Lao depots, and reporting to the Suranaree Task Force. The measures were framed as security controls intended to prevent onward export to third countries; the report does not establish that fuel had actually been diverted to Cambodia.

title: Cambodia seizes Thai trawler on encroachment charges
summary: Thai Newsroom, citing PPTVHD36, reported that Cambodian naval authorities seized the fishing boat K. Chok Burapha off Koh Kong on an alleged territorial-water encroachment, with about three tonnes of squid aboard. It said Thai and Cambodian maritime agencies were coordinating to verify ownership, route and other details.

title: Navy Checks Report on Fishing Vessel Ko Chok Burapha
summary: Thai PBS, citing Royal Thai Navy spokesperson Rear Adm Parat Rattanachaiyaphan, reported that at about 16:25 on February 14 Cambodian naval maritime inspectors were reported to have taken control of the fishing vessel Ko Chok Burapha in Pak Khlong, Koh Kong. The Navy said the former Thai registration had expired and the former registered owner said the vessel had been sold to a Cambodian national; the Navy was continuing to verify the report.

title: Si Sa Ket Senate Committee Visit in Phu Sing at Pha Phya Kouprey
summary: Thai Region News reported that on February 18 a Thai Senate extraordinary committee led by Noppadon Inna was welcomed at Pha Phya Kouprey, Ban Sae Prai, Phrai Phatthana subdistrict, Phu Sing district, Si Sa Ket, while studying Thai-Cambodian boundary issues and the pros and cons of ending the 2000 and 2001 MOUs. The report said provincial, district and military officials joined the visit.

title: Breaking: Army confirms landmine incident in Kantharalak, Si Sa Ket
summary: The Nation reported Thai Army and Second Army Area statements that at 16:40 on February 11 personnel from Infantry Company 132 were injured by an explosive device while conducting security and clearance work in Kantharalak district, Si Sa Ket. Private Pariwat Meemana lost his left lower leg, while two other soldiers were reported injured. Preliminary Thai reports said the device was believed to be an old landmine left from past fighting; the area was still being investigated.

title: Cambodia Reaffirms Mine Ban Commitments Following Reported Mine Discovery near Thai Border
summary: Cambodia's Mine Action and Victim Assistance Authority (CMAA) said on February 11 that, based on Cambodia's mine-action database and technical experience, any anti-personnel mine found in such border areas was highly likely to be a legacy device from past conflicts rather than newly emplaced. CMAA said Cambodia does not produce, stockpile or deploy anti-personnel mines and called for proper investigation before drawing conclusions.

title: Army Explains Soldier Injured by Old Landmine in Sisaket One Loses Left Leg, Three Injured, Prompt Medical Care Underway
summary: Thairath reported a Thai Army spokesperson as saying the Second Army Area received a report at about 16:40 on February 11 that personnel from Infantry Company 132 stepped on a landmine during a security mission in Kantharalak district, Si Sa Ket. Private Pariwat Meemana lost his left leg and suffered a severe right-leg wound; two other soldiers sustained minor injuries. The Army said the device was still under investigation and preliminary reports believed it to be an old explosive left from past fighting.

title: Second Army Reports Three Wildfire Points Near the Cambodia Border on February 22
summary: Naewna reported the Thai Second Army Region's February 22 wildfire update: three fire points were observed on the Cambodian side near Si Sa Ket, including two south of Khao Satta Som and one south of Prasat Don Tual. The Army said the Thai side remained able to control the situation and reported no spread into Thailand at Chong Bok or Chong An Ma.
